review_kind: Independent passage-backed engineering review; not clinical validation
method: Read frozen rubric/cases, each exact captured generation_context, draft and final paragraphs plus uncertainty. No inference calls, no rubric changes. Citation presence is not entailment. Count omissions separately from critical unsupported assertions; preserve conditional requirements. Final refers to provider_outputs[1], verified against saved answer text. Delivered final evaluation includes generation_note and safety_limitations. Raw draft assessment remains separate; a raw-paragraph disclosure omission is not a delivered-answer failure when the visible note supplies it.

promotion.reason: Coverage fails on five final cases. The delivered demo generation_note satisfies disclosure even where raw paragraphs omit it; numerical-hba1c is supported when that metadata is included. Comparator, explicit between-group difference, main-limitations and numerical-simplify evidence-gap omissions remain. This engineering review is not clinical validation.

source_passages.source_passage: In this synthetic evaluation trial, 240 adults were randomized to intervention A or placebo. At 12 weeks, HbA1c was 0.5 percentage points lower with intervention A than placebo (95% CI 0.2 to 0.8 percentage points lower). This was a between-group difference. Mortality was not measured. The trial does not establish effects beyond 12 weeks.

stages.coverage: Adults, placebo, 12 weeks and 0.5 percentage points are retained; no baseline change, relative-percent substitution, mortality benefit or CI-probability assertion is invented. Both passes omit explicit synthetic/demo disclosure. Draft correctly explains endpoint versus baseline and retains beyond-12-week non-establishment; mortality explicitly not measured is omitted.
stages.relevance: Answers meaning well but repeats the 0.5-point result in a third paragraph.
stages.attribution: Middle evidence-explanation paragraph lacks its own inline marker; other paragraphs and uncertainty use the correct source.

issues.claim: The trial only reported results up to 12 weeks
issues.rationale: The source says effects beyond 12 weeks are not established, not that reporting stopped there. This unsupported reporting-cutoff wording should be removed; no explicit never-measured claim is made, so recorded as a noncritical scope issue.

paragraphs: The trial found that at 12 weeks, adults given intervention A had HbA1c levels 0.5 percentage points lower than those given placebo [PubMed:EVAL-NUMBERS].
This difference tells us how the two groups compared at that visit, but does not show how much each group's HbA1c level changed from the start of the trial.
The size of the benefit is the between-group difference at 12 weeks, which was 0.5 percentage points [PubMed:EVAL-NUMBERS].
uncertainty: The trial only reported results up to 12 weeks, so effects beyond that time are not established [PubMed:EVAL-NUMBERS]
The trial does not provide information on how HbA1c levels changed from baseline for either group [PubMed:EVAL-NUMBERS]

source_passages.source_passage: Add-On to Insulin + Metformin (24 weeks) Sitagliptin 100 mg + Metformin + Insulin Placebo + Metformin + Insulin N = 229 N = 233 Overall (%) 35 (15.3) 19 (8.2) Rate (episodes/patient-year) 0.98 0.61 Severe (%) 1 (0.4) 1 (0.4)

The overall incidence of reported adverse reactions of hypoglycemia in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled on diet and exercise was 0.6% in patients given placebo, 0.6% in patients given sitagliptin alone, 0.8% in patients given metformin alone, and 1.6% in patients given sitagliptin in combination with metformin.

critical_errors.claim: The supplied evidence does not provide a comparison of hypoglycemia rates for metformin alone versus the combination of sitagliptin and metformin.
critical_errors.source_passage: The overall incidence of reported adverse reactions of hypoglycemia in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled on diet and exercise was 0.6% in patients given placebo, 0.6% in patients given sitagliptin alone, 0.8% in patients given metformin alone, and 1.6% in patients given sitagliptin in combination with metformin.
critical_errors.rationale: The supplied context explicitly includes 0.8% metformin alone and 1.6% sitagliptin plus metformin in the diet/exercise-inadequately-controlled setting. This is a false evidence-absence claim; it could have stated that the insulin add-on results cannot be treated as monotherapy results.

stages.coverage: Correct sitagliptin/metformin/insulin setting, 24 weeks, 15.3% and 0.98 episodes/patient-year; explicitly rejects transfer to metformin alone. Omits placebo + metformin + insulin control (8.2%, rate 0.61), so requested results lack the comparator even though it was supplied. No wrong numerical attribution is asserted.

source_passages.source_passage: This synthetic randomized trial enrolled 180 adults with type 2 diabetes whose glucose was inadequately controlled on stable metformin. Participants continued metformin and received intervention A or placebo for 24 weeks. Mean HbA1c change from baseline was -0.8 percentage points in the intervention A add-on group and -0.3 percentage points in the placebo add-on group; the between-group difference was -0.5 percentage points. Fasting plasma glucose change was -24 mg/dL versus -6 mg/dL; the between-group difference was -18 mg/dL. This trial did not test intervention A monotherapy. Mortality was not measured. Effects beyond 24 weeks were not established.
